completion:
Record the name and the address of the building.
3. Date and time of inspection.
4. Name of the inspector and their credentials.
5. Checklist used for inspection (path of travel, entrances, signage, parking, restrooms, elevators, ramps, etc.)
6. Detailed description of failed checks:
   a. Identify and describe the deficiency.
   b. Include measurements and precise locations where the issue arises.
   c. Use photographs and diagrams to show the noncompliance clearly.
   d. Detail how the failed check deviates from ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) guidelines or local building codes.
   e. Describe the accessibility impact on individuals with various disabilities (e.g., wheelchair users, visually impaired).
   f. Note if the issue presents an immediate safety risk.
